$schema_description: Machine-readable expected-outcome manifest for the RAMP resource-metadata round-trip corpus. DOCUMENTATION-ONLY: no runner currently loads this file or asserts against its `cases[*].expected` blocks — it records the intended per-line behaviour only. The executed guarantees live in Go integration tests: catalog_metadata_integration_test.go (Offer projection — an explicit resource_mutability is honored and not leaked to ext; an omitted value defaults to STATIC) and ingest_metadata_e2e_test.go (ingest parse/map layer). See README.md for the full scenario matrix. Wiring a runner that consumes this manifest is a separate follow-up.

conventions.file: JSONL fixture filename in this directory.
conventions.line_number: 1-based line within `file` (matches the parser's line numbering).
conventions.case_id: stable, descriptive identifier; assertion names derive from this.
conventions.expected.parse: "ok" when ParseJSONL accepts the line; {"reject": "<reason>", "layer": "parser|mapper"} when it must fail. `layer` says WHERE the reject lands once Record is extended: `parser` = Go json decode (DisallowUnknownFields / typed-field decode / trailing-content / RFC3339 decode); `mapper` = MapRecords token/enum validation after a clean parse.
conventions.expected.push: "accepted" when CatalogService.PushResources persists the entry; {"rejected": "<reason>"} when the push RPC (or the pre-push map step) rejects. For lines whose parse already fails, push is not reached; push is then null.
conventions.expected.offer: null when DiscoverResources yields no offer (e.g. parse/push rejected, or requester entitled to no priced term). Otherwise an object of field-level assertions on the signed Offer. Absent keys mean 'do not assert'. A key set to null asserts the Offer field is UNSET.
conventions.expected.offer.identity_content_hash: expected Offer.identity.content_hash (string) or null for unset.
conventions.expected.offer.identity_hash_method: expected Offer.identity.hash_method (string) or null for unset.
conventions.expected.offer.identity_resource_mutabil: expected Offer.identity.resource_mutability enum name; "RESOURCE_MUTABILITY_STATIC" (buildOffer default) when the feed omits the typed resource_mutability field. The typed ingest field is authoritative; a value in ext is not read.
conventions.expected.offer.previews: expected Offer.previews; either an integer count or an array of {url,media_type,width?,height?,duration?,size?} to assert proto-equal element-wise.
conventions.expected.offer.attestations: expected Offer.attestations; either an integer count or an array of {verifier,kid,attested_at,uri,claims,signature} to assert proto-equal.
conventions.expected.offer.ext: subset object that MUST be present (proto-equal) within Offer.ext; other ext keys may exist.
conventions.expected.offer.data_as_of: expected Offer.data_as_of as RFC3339; null asserts unset.
conventions.expected.offer.terms_unchanged: true asserts the projected Offer.terms set + order is identical to the metadata-free baseline for the same resource shape (entanglement invariant).
conventions.expected.offer.price_unchanged: true asserts Offer.pricing (model+rate+currency+unit) is identical to the metadata-free baseline (entanglement invariant).
conventions.expected.transact_parity: true => the e2e MUST drive ExecuteTransaction for this offer and assert the PRESENTED offer's signature re-verifies at execute (the signed bytes, metadata included, survive discovery -> presentation intact). false/absent => not exercised.

requester_profiles.default: no scopes (public). Used for every case unless the case names `requester`.
requester_profiles.premium: scopes:["subscription:premium"]. Used by the scope-projection premium cases.

cases.description: Happy path: every extended metadata field + a priced term. Every field must surface on the Offer.
Only content_hash + hash_method present; all other metadata unset on the Offer.
Only provenance fields + source present; data_as_of set, identity hashes unset.
Only the typed resource_mutability present; sets Offer.identity.resource_mutability=DYNAMIC, nothing else.

files.note: One line per IngestionSource enum value (UNSPECIFIED excluded: it is the absent default, covered by legacy_zero_metadata). `source` is an ingest-side audit field on ResourceEntry; it has no dedicated typed Offer field, so the Offer assertion is that the line round-trips (offer present, terms/price unchanged). The e2e MAY additionally assert the persisted catalog row's source via the black-box transaction-log/catalog read exception.

files.note: Each line is invalid in EXACTLY ONE way. `layer` records where the reject lands once Record is extended (see conventions). Lines whose parse fails never reach push (push=null).

cases.description: Genuinely-unknown top-level key `totally_unknown_field`. DisallowUnknownFields must stay strict.

provenance_timestamp not RFC3339 ("18.03.2026 09:30"). Parser keeps provenance_timestamp as a raw string (pure DTO); the mapper validates it via time.Parse(RFC3339) and rejects, so layer is mapper (consistent with reject_garbage_source).
source=INGESTION_SOURCE_TELEPATHY is not a real IngestionSource value. Rejected at the mapper enum resolution (source decodes as a string at parse, fails enum lookup at map time).

ext is a JSON string, not an object. The parser models ext as json.RawMessage, which accepts any valid JSON including a bare string, so the parser does NOT reject. The mapper rejects when converting ext to *structpb.Struct (protojson.Unmarshal of a JSON string into a Struct fails), so layer is mapper (consistent with reject_garbage_source / reject_malformed_provenance_timestamp).

parse.reject: ext must be a JSON object

cases.description: attestations[0].claims is a JSON string, not an object. The parser models attestation.claims as json.RawMessage, which accepts any valid JSON including a bare string, so the parser does NOT reject. The mapper rejects when converting claims to *structpb.Struct, so layer is mapper.

parse.reject: attestation claims must be a JSON object

cases.description: Trailing content after the JSON object. ParseJSONL's dec.More() guard rejects.

parse.reject: unexpected trailing content after JSON object

files.note: Both lines PARSE cleanly (resource_mutability is a known typed field) but are rejected at the MAPPER's enum resolution, mirroring reject_garbage_source: an explicit RESOURCE_MUTABILITY_UNSPECIFIED trips the {not_in:[0]} mirror, and an unknown name fails the enum-value lookup. MapRecords short-circuits, so a batch containing either persists NOTHING.

cases.description: Explicit resource_mutability=RESOURCE_MUTABILITY_UNSPECIFIED. Rejected at mapResourceMutability (the ingest mirror of the Offer-side {not_in:[0]} rule).
resource_mutability=RESOURCE_MUTABILITY_TELEPATHY is not a real ResourceMutability value; fails the enum-value lookup at the mapper.

file_level_expectation.description: A 3-line file where line 1 and line 3 are valid but line 2 is invalid (per_unit pricing with no unit -> mapPricing reject in MapRecords, before the PushResources RPC). The ingest run MUST fail as a whole and persist NOTHING: after the failed run, DiscoverResources for /article/aon-valid-before AND /article/aon-valid-after MUST both yield no offer. This proves the batch is all-or-nothing -- a single bad line voids the entire push, including the otherwise-valid lines around it.

run.rejected: term 0: per_unit pricing requires a unit (line 2)

The single bad line: per_unit pricing missing unit.
Valid line following the bad one; MUST NOT be persisted because the batch fails.

files.note: ENTANGLEMENT/pass-through invariant pair. Both lines carry an IDENTICAL terms[] block (same license, same per_unit term, same quota). Line 1 additionally carries the full metadata payload; line 2 carries none. The e2e MUST assert that the SELECTED term and the price (model+rate+currency+unit) are IDENTICAL across the two resulting offers -- metadata is inert to the Exchange's scope projection (selectTerms). This is the core proof that adding metadata does not change which term/price is chosen.

cases.description: Resource WITH full metadata; selected term + price must match the no-meta twin.
Same resource WITHOUT metadata; defines the baseline selected term + price the with-meta twin must equal.

pairwise_assertion.description: Cross-line assertion: offer(passthrough_baseline_with_meta).pricing == offer(passthrough_baseline_without_meta).pricing AND the selected term (terms[0]) is proto-equal across the two offers. Metadata MUST NOT alter term/price selection.

files.note: ENTANGLEMENT invariant under scope projection. The resource carries TWO enumerated terms in this order: [0] premium (scopes:["subscription:premium"], flat 9.99), [1] public (no scopes, flat 4.99). The SAME metadata must be emitted on the Offer regardless of which term the Exchange's scope projection (selectTerms) keeps for the requester. Run this line TWICE: once with the `premium` requester (selects term[0], price 9.99) and once with the `default` requester (term[0] filtered out, selects the public term, price 4.99). Metadata fields are identical in both offers; only the selected term/price differs -- driven by scopes ONLY, never by metadata.

cases.description: premium requester -> premium term selected (9.99); full metadata present.
default (no-scope) requester -> premium term filtered out, public term selected (4.99); SAME metadata present.

pairwise_assertion.description: Cross-requester assertion on the SAME line: metadata (identity hashes, mutability, previews, attestations, data_as_of) is proto-equal between the premium-requester offer and the default-requester offer, while selected_price_rate differs (9.99 vs 4.99). Proves metadata projection is independent of scope-driven term selection.

cases.description: Metadata-bearing line driven through the full push -> discover -> ExecuteTransaction path. After discovery returns the signed offer, the e2e calls ExecuteTransaction with that offer; the Exchange verifies the PRESENTED offer's exact signed bytes and the signature MUST re-verify -- i.e. the metadata the discovery path signed (identity hashes, mutability, previews, attestations, ext, ext_critical, data_as_of) reaches execute byte-identical. This is the signature-parity assertion that guards against metadata being included in discovery but dropped (or reordered) between signing and presentation.
